evidence.text: Global smartphone shipments fell 20% YoY in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint) or 22% to 255.3M units (IDC preliminary), the weakest Q3 since 2012, driven by DRAM/NAND costs. IDC sees 2026 down 16.7%, and Counterpoint sees no volume recovery until component costs ease (possibly late 2027). Amkor's communications segment was 42% of Q2 sales. Amkor guided Q3 communications down high single digits QoQ and said Android revenue fell 20% QoQ in Q2 on memory. Apple, Amkor's largest communications customer, gained share from 18% to 22%, so Apple units were roughly flat YoY. The read is worse for Android than for Amkor's Apple-heavy mix. For the Q4 guide, the memory squeeze has no visible end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: guided communications down high single digits and Q3 revenue about 5% below consensus, and the stock fell 24.74%. The communications line moves this stock.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Zacks consensus already models communications at 36% of Q3 sales against 51% a year earlier, which implies communications revenue down about 28% YoY, and the stock fell about 28% after these data. The open question is the Q4 communications guide, where the derived consensus has total Q4 flat on Q3.
evidence.independence: Counterpoint (https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/global-smartphone-shipments-hit-a-14-year-low-in-q3-amid-a-memory-shortage-561272-2026-10-13) and IDC agree. Amkor's own July call cited memory constraints. It shares the memory-cost cause with the iPhone finding below but is a different data set (global units against Apple Pro orders).

evidence.text: Q3 EPS carries the semi-annual coupon on Bladex's $200M 7.50% AT1 notes (issued September 2025), which is deducted from profit attributable to common shareholders. That is about $7.5M, or roughly $0.20 a share on ~36.6M shares. In Q1 2026 the same deduction took EPS to $1.31 (-13% QoQ, -7% YoY) while net profit rose 9% YoY to $56.4M, and the stock fell 5.9% the next day (56.64 to 53.29). Q2 (EPS $1.77 on $66.5M) and Q4 (EPS $1.50 on $56.0M) show almost no deduction, so the coupon falls in Q1 and Q3. A Q3 net profit equal to Q2's would still print EPS near $1.57, against a FY-consensus-implied run rate of about $1.70.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last quarter with this deduction (Q1 2026, reported 2026-04-27 amc) traded -5.9% next day on an EPS decline with net profit up YoY; the quarters without it (Q4 2025 +3.0%, Q2 2026 +1.1%) traded up.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is mechanical and the two covering analysts may model it, but the aggregated FY EPS consensus of 6.47 implies H2 EPS of 3.39, which only works if net profit stays near Q2's record despite the deduction. If the deduction were priced, FY consensus would sit nearer the guidance-implied ~6.1, as the low estimate does. Headline-EPS screens will show a sharp QoQ drop from $1.77.

evidence.text: Bladex closed (2026-09-09) and announced (2026-09-15) a term financing of up to $1.0bn to the Republic of Panama (MEF), its largest transaction ever 'structured and granted'. Molina's Q3 (Oct 21) had Medicaid MCR 93.0% and Marketplace MCR 92.5%, both 'in line', and reaffirmed guidance. UNH (Oct 13) beat at $4.69 vs about $4.14 and raised. Centene's own Q2 call said the 7/1 rate cohort (about 20% of Medicaid members) gives a Q2-to-Q3 sequential benefit, and guided Q3 to 'a little above breakeven' against a street of about $0.09. The read-through points to a Q3 above that bar.

Q1 2026: $3.37, about $0.50 above expectations, stock +13.95%. Q3 2025: beat and raise, +12.5%. A quarter beat pays only when the outlook is not dimmed.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q3 street ($0.08-0.09) and revenue ($47B) were 'generally unchanged over the last 30 days' per StockStory, so the estimates have not absorbed the peer prints. The stock has, though: +13.5% in a month. That is why this is sized small.

evidence.text: The 2027 ACA marketplace has competitors leaving and rates going up while Centene holds its footprint. Cigna, Molina, CareSource, Baylor Scott & White and Providence are exiting, which affects 'hundreds of thousands' of enrollees. Centene adds 55 counties in AL, IA, IL, LA, MI, NJ and TX and exits DE and NH, net flat on 3.5M+ enrollees. KFF puts the median proposed 2027 premium increase at about 15%. On the Q2 call management said it would give 'more clarity on the Q3 call' on 2027 marketplace positioning and margin restoration.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace is the line that broke the stock: the 2025-07-01 risk-adjustment pull was -40.37%. Marketplace margin raised from 3% to 4.5-5% at Q2 2026 (-0.27%, offset by the Medicaid outlook). Commentary in March 2026 that ACA membership would fall was followed by about -18%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The footprint is public, but how much of the competitor exits Centene captures, and at what margin, only comes out when management speaks on the call. If it were priced, the 2027 revenue consensus ($192.75B) would not sit below 2026 ($195.9B). Partly priced through the run-up.
evidence.independence: KFF 2027 rate-filing analysis (https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/how-much-and-why-aca-marketplace-premiums-are-going-up-in-2027/) is a separate source. evidence.text: Both Medicaid peers that reported after Centene last spoke are constructive on 2027 Medicaid rates. Molina's CEO: 'the strength of recent rate updates for 2027 ... we believe we are likely observing the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins.' Elevance is 'encouraged by early 2027 rates', calls 2026 the trough, and describes Medicaid as 'moving from stabilization to improvement'. Centene's Q2 call said OB3 would 'mute' its Medicaid recovery into 2027, with acceleration only in H2 2027, which is the line it was sold on in July. Peer evidence of strong 1/1/2027 rates gives the Q3 call room to firm that language.

evidence.text: Centene's 2027 Medicare Star Ratings (released by CMS around Oct 9, 2026) fell: Stephens puts 9% of members in 4+ star plans vs 18% for 2026, and Becker's has the unweighted average down from 3.31 to 3.14. Industry-wide, 4+ star enrollment rose from about 64% to 71%. This cuts 2028 MA quality bonuses and makes the 'MA breakeven or better in 2027, margin improvement after' path harder. Management flagged Stars as a risk on the Q2 call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sept 2025: preliminary Stars 'in line' with a slightly higher 4-star share moved the stock up sharply (Bloomberg Law 2025-09-11). The MA segment is about 1M members and small next to Medicaid and PDP.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and the stock rose about 13% after it, so it is mostly priced. What remains is whether management quantifies a 2028 headwind on the call. It affects 2028, so only a small piece can move this window.
evidence.independence: Becker's '8 things to know about 2027 MA star ratings' (https://www.beckerspayer.com/?p=29667), which reports the same direction (3.31 to 3.14).

evidence.text: The 2026-to-2027 bridge is demanding against a single-source FY2027 street of $5.35, which is +10% on the FY2026 street of $4.88 and about +22% once the roughly $0.50 of 2026 non-recurring Q2 settlements is removed ($180M marketplace risk adjustment, $160M Medicare), which management said will not recur. Expansion members are about 18% of Medicaid by year-end, with mid-single-digit attrition expected over 2027-28. CMS's RIA for the June 2026 work-requirement IFR projects -2.3M Medicaid enrollment in FY2027, and requirements start 2027-01-01. The PDP premium stabilization demo ends after 2026. The Q3 call is where management promised 2027 detail.

evidence.why_not_priced: If the street had absorbed the bridge, FY2027 EPS would sit near $4.4-4.9, not at $5.35, and the stock would not be 4.6% from its high after +13.5% in a month. The skew (+5 puts bid) suggests options already hedge some of this. The bar is single-source, so this is capped.

evidence.text: The Q4 outlook the call will be asked about is soft. Industry inventory reached about 572k t at end-September and is expected to keep building in October. Polysilicon futures were RMB 34,285/t on Oct 16 against RMB 43,000/t spot, about 20% lower, so the futures market does not believe spot will hold. Only 2-3 companies transacted in the week to Oct 21, and buyers are waiting. Daqo told investors on Oct 8-9 that it will set production according to supply and demand, which makes a Q4 production guide below Q3's 40-45k MT likely, with higher unit fixed cost.

evidence.text: FY2026 PSUs vested at 100% of target, which is the maximum since the FY26 plan has no overachievement. EVP Velasco earned 4,666 PSUs on 2026-10-16 against a 4,667-share restricted-stock half of the same FY26 grant (Form 4, 2025-09-04), and CEO David Price earned 11,457. Half of the FY26 metric is total revenue or constant-currency net merchandise sales and half is EPS (DEF 14A), so the compensation committee had seen final FY26 numbers clear both the revenue and the EPS targets ten days before the release. In FY25 the same determination (2025-10-17) vested only 27.4%: NMS of $5,151M missed the $5,200M threshold and adjusted operating income of $237.6M was just over the $236.3M floor. That print missed EPS by $0.04 and fell 6.48%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 (2025-10-30), when the FY PSU vested at 27.4% and EPS missed by $0.04: -6.48%. Q3 FY26 EPS beat ($1.28 vs $1.23): -0.45%. Q2 FY26: +2.91%. Q1 FY26: +4.55%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Form 4 footnote reads only 'target criteria determined to have been met'. Seeing that this is a 100% (maximum) vest needs three documents joined: the FY26 RSA count from Sept 2025, the no-overachievement design in the DEF 14A, and the FY25 27.4% comparison. No aggregator carries that join. Had it been priced, the stock would not sit flat and 13% under its high into the print. The limit is that the board's EPS target is unpublished and may sit below consensus, so this rules out a bad year more than it proves a beat.
evidence.independence: Same filer family: David Price's Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1041803/000162828026066544/wk-form4_1792531287.xml) shows 11,457 PSUs earned against 1,311 for FY25. evidence.text: Montage Technology, Rambus's largest competitor in DDR5 RCD and memory interface chips, pre-announced Q3 2026 on 2026-10-20. Interconnect-chip revenue was about RMB 2.047bn, +20.9% QoQ and +49.3% YoY, after about +20% QoQ in Q2. Interconnect gross margin was 68.0-68.5%, up 0.6-1.1 points QoQ. Management said Q4 interconnect demand will rise further, citing a rising mix of 3rd-5th generation RCD. Rambus guided Q3 product revenue to $110-116m, +14% QoQ at the midpoint off $99.2m. If the buffer-chip market grew about 20% QoQ in Q3 and Rambus held share, product revenue lands at or above the top of its guide ($116m), and a Q4 product guide up QoQ is more likely than the flat-to-down Q4 the Baird 'shortage caps units' thesis implies.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product revenue has beaten repeatedly without being paid. Q2 2026 product revenue was $99.2m (+13% QoQ) and total revenue beat the top of guidance, yet the stock fell 8.99%; Q1 2026 was a solid beat and fell 21.26% on a downgrade about 2027 units. The last four prints fell -8.71, -13.42, -21.26 and -8.99 (baseline). What has moved the stock is the forward unit narrative, so this finding is filed on guidance.
evidence.why_not_priced: RMBS fell 5.1% in the five sessions after Montage's pre-announcement and sits 10% above its 52-week low, with put skew bid. If the market had carried Montage's +21% QoQ and its Q4 demand comment over to Rambus, the stock would have rallied off the 10/20 print, not drifted down into its own. The pre-announcement was in Chinese and HK/Shanghai coverage, with no English Rambus preview citing it that I could find. Caveat: Montage's growth may include share gains at Rambus's expense, since Montage cites a rising share of new-generation RCD. Rambus's own guide already embeds +14% QoQ, so only the gap of roughly 6 points of product growth (about $6m, ~3% of revenue) is new.

evidence.text: Server CPU demand, which drives RCD units, was very strong per direct customers of the ecosystem. Intel's Q2 2026 DCAI revenue rose 59% YoY to $6.3bn, with Xeon demand outrunning supply partly because of memory and substrate shortages (reported July 2026). Micron's FQ4 2026 (2026-09-30) forecast server units growing in the high teens and said over 75% of FY27 shipments are under allocation or contract. Both point to RCD unit demand above supply, not below it, in H2 2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. The market has repeatedly treated strong server demand as already priced for RMBS; Q2 'H2 stronger than H1' commentary still sold off 9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are public macro prints from July and September. It is filed as a small proxy because it is macro-to-company transmission that Rambus itself has not confirmed. If it were unpriced, RMBS would not be 48% off its high while Micron reports records.
evidence.independence: Intel Q2 2026 DCAI +59% YoY with demand ahead of supply, summarised in search coverage of Intel's July 2026 print. The Nasdaq article https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/intel-just-delivered-investors-here-are-6-key-things-know is from a different source than Micron. It shares the demand thesis with the Montage finding but rests on different documents.

evidence.text: The bear thesis on units is live and sourced. TrendForce (July 2026) projects RDIMM supply growing only 15-20% in 2027, well behind server CPU supply, implying an RDIMM shortage in 2027. Its July server DIMM report notes short-term inventory rising because processor shortages delay server assembly and buyers stockpile. Fusion Worldwide reports servers shipping with little or no memory installed. This is the Baird downgrade thesis of 2026-04-28 (RMBS cannot raise prices in a shortage, and units are capped), and it is what a 2027 or Q4 commentary could confirm.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line moved the stock -21.26% on 2026-04-28, when Baird cut to Neutral on 2027 RDIMM growth slowing from DRAM shortages (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/28/why-rambus-plunged-today/). In each of the last four prints the forward/2027 narrative dominated a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the consensus bear case behind a stock 48% off its high and with put skew bid. What remains unpriced is whether management quantifies a 2027 RDIMM unit constraint on the call, which would be new. If it were fully priced, a strong Montage print would have lifted RMBS, and it did not.
evidence.independence: Fusion Worldwide, RDIMM shortages blog, https://info.fusionww.com/blog/rdimm-shortages-and-the-shift-in-server-shipments (different source, same thesis). This partly contradicts finding 2. They are reconciled into one direction: demand above supply means Q3/Q4 revenue is supported, while 2027 unit growth is the risk.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 brought a large rate and credit-spread shock to SoFi's fair-value loan book. The 2-year Treasury rose from 4.17% on 2026-06-30 to 4.85% on 2026-09-30 (+68bp; Equibles measures +74bp), the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-17, and HY spreads widened from 2.75% to 3.12%, which the hedges do not cover. Exposure at June 30 was $29.7B of loans held for sale at fair value plus $16.9B held for investment at fair value. KBW (Underperform, target cut to $15 in mid-October) estimates the Q3 rate move costs more than $1B before hedges. For comparison, Q2 absorbed only a 37bp benchmark rise. Equibles models a net fair-value result of +$130M (hedges included), against a $100M downside case. The rate damage is outside what was guided only to the extent the 2-year moved by more than the 1-2 hikes the guide assumed. With the 10-year at about 5.1% in mid-October and October hike odds near 50% after the Oct 14 CPI print, Q4 marks and the guide carry the same risk.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-04-29 the stock fell 15.4% when the guide was held because no rate cuts were expected (secondary source). On 2026-07-29 it fell 8.9% even though Q2 absorbed a 37bp benchmark rise and still beat revenue by 5.5%. Rate headwinds have hit this name through the guide rather than through the reported revenue line, which SoFi has beaten every quarter.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. KBW's note is public, the stock made 52-week lows on Oct 14-15 on the CPI and rates move, and skew is +10.5. What may not be priced is the exact net mark: if the HY-spread widening flows into SoFi's discount rate unhedged, the reported lending line could absorb a hit of $100M or more, which nobody has published. If the market had fully priced a large net mark, consensus revenue would have been cut. Instead it is flat at $1.26B, above the guide's implied H2 run-rate.
evidence.independence: The rate path is confirmed separately by Mortgage News Daily's June 30 2-year close of 4.173% (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com/treasury/2yr) and the late-September level of ~4.79-4.85% (https://cryptobriefing.com/two-year-treasury-yields-climb-toward-5-percent/, 2026-09-23).
